words.sense: To dwell on something excessively to the point of tedium.
words.concise_meaning: To unnecessarily repeat or dwell on known information.
misconceptions: mistakenly thinking it relates to 'working hard' (labor)

words.sense: To explain something by adding useful, clarifying detail.
words.concise_meaning: To explain by adding helpful, new detail.

semantic_axes.description: Whether the added information genuinely enhances understanding or is merely redundant.
Whether the audience is enlightened (positive) or bored and frustrated (negative).

edge.boundary_rule: Is the added detail useful for comprehension (elaborate) or redundant/tedious repetition of what is already known (belabor)?
clues_a: excessive time spent on simple concepts
irrelevant_clues: the volume or speed of speaking
the length of the explanation if it's actually adding new useful facts

misconceptions.M1: Confusing belabor with literal physical labor.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming elaborate always means something fancy or complicated.
misconceptions.M3: Ignoring the utility of the detail.

belabor: He continued to belabor the point even after the group had unanimously agreed.
Please stop belaboring the obvious facts; we all understand.
The professor tended to belabor simple concepts, frustrating advanced students.
There is no need to belabor the details of our agreement; they are clear.
She felt the candidate was belaboring the issue instead of offering solutions.
Don't belabor the argument; it’s already settled.
elaborate: Could you elaborate on your proposal for the new marketing strategy?
The expert was asked to elaborate on the findings of her latest research.
She began to elaborate on the design features of the prototype.
The teacher helped the class by elaborating on the difficult historical process.
They needed more time to elaborate on the technical explanation.
Please elaborate on what you meant by 'urgent'.

belabor: She belabor on the complex design perfectly.
The project team belabored their proposal until it was clear to everyone.
He successfully belabored his theory during the lecture.
The architect belabored the blueprint for hours until it was complete.
They were asked to belabor on the results.
I appreciate you belaboring the solution.
elaborate: He continued to elaborate on the point even after the group had unanimously agreed.
Please stop elaborating on the obvious facts; we all understand.
The professor tended to elaborate on simple concepts, frustrating advanced students.
There is no need to elaborate on the details of our agreement; they are clear.
She felt the candidate was elaborating the issue instead of offering solutions.
Don't elaborate the argument; it’s already settled.

borderline.text: The scientist needed to _________ the complex data to ensure the interns understood.
borderline.note: Here, it's about making complex data understandable (adding useful detail), not repeating the obvious.

borderline.text: The speaker continued to _________ the already trivial point, losing the entire audience.
borderline.note: The point was trivial and already known; dwelling on it is clearly tedious.

borderline.text: Please _________ on your initial thought; it’s a promising start.
borderline.note: Adding detail to a promising start is clearly beneficial.

borderline.text: Despite having made his position perfectly clear, he kept _________ the point for another ten minutes.
borderline.note: Ten minutes of repeating an already clear position is the definition of tedious.

chains.frame: What the manager is doing to the budget discussion: ___

beats.text: The manager went over the budget again, although everyone already agreed.
beats.reason: The manager is dwelling on a resolved point, which is tedious.

beats.text: He spent another twenty minutes explaining why the ink costs were too high, adding nothing we didn't know.
beats.reason: Reinforces the repetitive/unnecessary nature of the action.

chains.feedback_short: The manager is repeating known information, not adding new, useful details.
chains.feedback_deep: The manager is going over the budget again, despite everyone agreeing. He is adding no new information and is just wasting time by repeating known points. This is a classic case of dwelling on something until it becomes tedious, which fits belabor.
chains.contrast_rule: If the information is already known, you belabor it; if it's new and useful, you elaborate.
chains.hint: Is the manager adding new information or just repeating?

chains.frame: How the student is handling her proposal: ___

beats.text: The student provided a brief outline of the new study, though it lacked clarity.
beats.reason: The student needs to add detail to improve understanding.

beats.text: She followed up by adding specific research methodology and sample size targets that truly filled the gap.
beats.reason: The added detail is useful and clarifies the proposal.

chains.feedback_short: The student is adding missing, helpful details to clarify the project.
chains.feedback_deep: The student's initial outline lacked clarity, so she added specific methodology and sample size targets. This is exactly what it means to elaborate—providing necessary information to improve understanding, not repeating what is already known.
chains.contrast_rule: Elaborate adds useful depth; belabor dwells on the known.
chains.hint: Does the student's detail help or hinder?

chains.frame: How the writer is presenting his main argument: ___

beats.text: The writer keeps explaining the premise of the book, which we already understood perfectly.
He just added a crucial missing fact about the author's intent that clarified everything.
beats.reason: The new detail is helpful, so he is elaborating.

chains.feedback_short: The focus shifted from unnecessary repetition to providing a crucial missing fact.
chains.feedback_deep: Initially, the writer was repeating a premise we already understood (belabor). However, adding the crucial missing fact about the author's intent provided new, useful information that improved understanding (elaborate). The goal changed from being tedious to being helpful.
chains.contrast_rule: If it adds crucial new information, it's not belaboring.
chains.hint: Does the second beat add anything necessary?

chains.frame: How the politician is addressing the question: ___

beats.text: The politician refused to answer the direct question, instead rephrasing the same basic stance.
beats.reason: Repeating the same stance instead of giving new information is belaboring.

beats.text: He then repeated the same stance for the fourth time, even after the host asked for new data.

chains.feedback_short: The politician is stubbornly repeating the same stance instead of providing new data.
chains.feedback_deep: Repeating the same basic stance repeatedly, even when asked for new data, is the definition of belaboring a point. It's a refusal to add new, useful information, turning the explanation into something tedious for the listener.
chains.contrast_rule: If it's just repeating what's already been said, it's belaboring.
chains.hint: Is the politician providing anything fresh?

chains.frame: How the chef is explaining his recipe: ___

beats.text: The chef described how to whisk the eggs until fluffy, but he was missing a few steps.
He added that you should use a stainless steel bowl and ice bath, which really helped.

chains.feedback_short: The chef provided helpful, clarifying details on the recipe.
chains.feedback_deep: The chef initially missed steps, but adding the advice to use a stainless steel bowl and ice bath (useful, new details) clarified the recipe and made it easier for the listener to follow. This is a clear case of elaborating.
chains.contrast_rule: Useful detail is elaborating; redundant detail is belaboring.
chains.hint: Does the chef's extra info help?

chains.frame: How the debater is presenting his stance: ___

beats.text: The debater provided a clear initial position and then added a new, compelling case study.
beats.decisive_clue: added a new, compelling case study
beats.reason: Adding new detail that improves the argument is elaborating.

beats.text: For the rest of the time, he just kept rehashing that same case study over and over.
beats.decisive_clue: rehashing that same case study over and over
beats.reason: Repeating the same information is belaboring.

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from adding a useful study to just repeating it tediously.
chains.feedback_deep: He started well by adding a useful case study to his argument (elaborate). But then he switched to just rehashing the same information, which is the definition of belaboring a point—making the argument tedious by repeating what's already been heard.
chains.contrast_rule: Adding new information is elaborating; repeating the same info is belaboring.
chains.hint: What changed after the case study?

chains.frame: How the lab tech is describing the procedure: ___

beats.text: The lab tech explained the procedure to the new interns, clarifying each step.
She added a list of specific safety protocols that the interns hadn't considered.
beats.reason: Adding helpful safety protocols is elaborating.

chains.feedback_short: She added genuinely helpful, necessary information.
chains.feedback_deep: The lab tech was already elaborating by clarifying steps, but adding safety protocols that the interns hadn't considered made it even more clearly an act of adding useful information. Both steps were about enhancing understanding.
chains.contrast_rule: Adding useful, new depth is always elaborating.
chains.hint: Is the new information helpful or redundant?

chains.frame: How the director is discussing the project goals: ___

beats.text: The director told the team to increase sales, but didn't say how.
beats.reason: The explanation is too vague, but not yet tedious.

beats.text: He just kept repeating 'increase sales' for twenty minutes without any further guidance.
beats.reason: The repetition of a vague point is tedious.

chains.feedback_short: Repeating a vague point without any additional guidance is tedious.
chains.feedback_deep: The director began by being unhelpful, and then he made it worse by repeating the vague goal for twenty minutes without adding any actual instruction. This is belaboring—it's repetitive, uninformative, and ultimately frustrating for the audience.
chains.contrast_rule: Repeating the same thing without adding detail is belaboring.

chains.frame: How the critic is describing the painting: ___

beats.text: The art critic spent a long time describing the colors in the landscape, adding technical details about the pigments.
beats.decisive_clue: adding technical details about the pigments

beats.text: He then went on to describe the brushwork in a similarly detailed way for another twenty minutes.
beats.reason: Still providing useful, albeit long, information.

chains.feedback_short: The detail is long, but it remains useful and distinct from repetition.
chains.feedback_deep: Even though twenty minutes is a long time, the critic is providing distinct technical details about the brushwork, which is different from repeating the pigment information. It's still a form of elaboration, not repetition.
chains.contrast_rule: Detailed explanation, no matter how long, is not belaboring if it's not repetitive.
chains.hint: Is he repeating the same information or providing new, distinct detail?

chains.frame: How the teacher is describing the science experiment: ___

beats.text: The teacher described the experiment but skipped the safety step, leaving students confused.
She then went back and added that specific safety step, which resolved the confusion.

chains.feedback_short: She added a crucial, clarifying piece of information.
chains.feedback_deep: The teacher went back to add the specific safety step she had initially missed. This is exactly what it means to elaborate—providing missing, useful information to complete the explanation and clear up confusion. It's not repetition.
chains.contrast_rule: Fixing a missing detail is elaborating.
chains.hint: Was the addition necessary for understanding?

chains.frame: How the lawyer is presenting his case to the jury: ___

beats.text: The lawyer laid out the evidence clearly and concisely.
He then proceeded to talk about the same evidence for two more hours, simply repeating the same points in slightly different ways.

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from clarity to tedious repetition of the same points.
chains.feedback_deep: The lawyer started well, but two hours of repeating the same points is the classic definition of belaboring. It turns a clear, concise presentation into something tedious and unproductive for the jury.
chains.contrast_rule: Repetition makes it belabor; clarity makes it elaborate.
chains.hint: What changed after the initial clear explanation?

chains.frame: How the developer is describing the new feature: ___

beats.text: The developer explained how the new feature would improve user experience, but it was still a bit abstract.
He provided a specific example of how it would reduce load times by two seconds.

chains.feedback_short: He provided a specific example that made the abstract explanation concrete.
chains.feedback_deep: The developer initially provided an abstract explanation. Adding a specific example about reducing load times is a perfect example of elaborating—providing useful, concrete detail to make the explanation more understandable.
chains.contrast_rule: Specific examples are great tools to elaborate.
chains.hint: Does the specific example make the feature clearer?

chains.frame: How Mark is dealing with his past disagreement with Sarah: ___

beats.text: Mark brought up the argument from last week, although Sarah thought it was resolved.
He spent an hour rehashing every single sentence from that night, even though she already knew his position perfectly well.

chains.feedback_short: Rehashing resolved arguments that the other person already understands is tedious.
chains.feedback_deep: Mark is repeating information Sarah already understands perfectly, turning a resolved argument into something tedious to discuss. This is a clear case of belaboring the point, which is damaging to the relationship.
chains.contrast_rule: If you are repeating what they already know, you are belaboring it.
chains.hint: Is Sarah learning anything new from Mark's repetition?

chains.frame: How the coach is giving instructions to his team: ___

beats.text: The coach explained the new defensive formation, but the players seemed unsure.
He then demonstrated how each player should pivot and communicate, which helped them understand perfectly.

chains.feedback_short: He provided a demonstration that clarified the new formation.
chains.feedback_deep: The coach initially failed to make the formation clear, but by demonstrating the pivots and communication, he provided useful, clarifying information that allowed the players to understand. This is a classic example of elaborating.
chains.contrast_rule: A demonstration to clarify understanding is elaborating.
chains.hint: Did the demonstration help the players?

chains.frame: How the tour guide is describing the old castle: ___

beats.text: The guide gave a quick, general overview of the castle's history, but people asked for more details.
He then insisted on talking about the same room for the entire duration of the tour, ignoring other areas.

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from being helpful to being tedious and repetitive.
chains.feedback_deep: Initially, the guide was about to be helpful by adding details, but he instead got stuck on one single room for the entire tour, ignoring the rest. This became tedious, turning his guide service into something repetitive and frustrating.
chains.contrast_rule: Spending the whole tour on one point is belaboring.
chains.hint: What changed when he focused on only one room?

chains.frame: How the person is fixing the leaking tap: ___

beats.text: He explained that the washer needs replacing, and gave a helpful list of tools needed.
For the next hour, he just kept talking about the same washer over and over, while the sink remained unfixed.
beats.decisive_clue: talking about the same washer over and over

chains.feedback_short: He switched from being helpful to repeating the same point tediously.
chains.feedback_deep: He began by providing helpful details about tools (elaborate), but then he spent an hour repeating the same thing about the washer without fixing anything. This is a clear case of belaboring the point, making the explanation tedious.
chains.contrast_rule: If you're not doing anything and just repeating, you're belaboring.
chains.hint: Did his repetition help fix the tap?

chains.frame: How the announcer is handling the delay: ___

beats.text: The announcer informed the passengers about the delay and explained the technical issue clearly.
He then spent the next hour repeating the same vague excuse, ignoring all the passengers' questions.

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from being informative to being tediously repetitive.
chains.feedback_deep: The announcer was initially informative (elaborate), but repeating the same vague excuse for an hour is a classic case of belaboring. It stops being informative and starts being tedious for the passengers.
chains.contrast_rule: Informative detail is elaborate; repetitive excuse is belabor.
chains.hint: What changed from the first to the second announcement?

chains.frame: How the philosopher is presenting his theory: ___

beats.text: The philosopher presented the theory and added new evidence that proved his point.
He then spent hours talking about that same evidence, adding nothing new to his argument.

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from adding new evidence to tediously repeating it.
chains.feedback_deep: The philosopher was initially elaborating by providing useful new evidence. But spending hours talking about that same evidence without adding anything new turns it into a tedious repetition, which is belaboring the point.
chains.contrast_rule: If it adds nothing new, it's not elaborating.
chains.hint: Did the hours of extra talking add new insight?

chains.frame: How the student is handling the question: ___

beats.text: Student A: 'I'm not sure how this formula works.' Student B: 'Let me break it down into smaller parts for you.'
beats.decisive_clue: break it down into smaller parts

beats.text: Student B: 'See? Part A does this. And Part A does this. And Part A does this.'

chains.feedback_short: He shifted from breaking it down to repeating the same part.
chains.feedback_deep: Student B initially tried to elaborate by breaking it down. But then, by repeating the same Part A three times without moving forward, he made the explanation tedious, which is the essence of belaboring a point.
chains.contrast_rule: Breaking it down is elaborating; repeating the same part is belaboring.
chains.hint: What changed in how Student B explained Part A?
